reden: Yes. The audit explicitly reports that burn() performs external token transfers before updating liquidityBalances/totalSupply/reserves, enabling reentrancy via token callbacks (ERC777-style) while state is stale, and under pre-0.8 arithmetic the subsequent unchecked subtractions can underflow/wrap. It even outlines the attack of reentering burn() to get paid multiple times. This is the same vulnerability as the description: reentrancy in FeeAMM.sol burn() due to CEI violation, allowing pool drainage. The same fix (move state updates before transfers or add a reentrancy guard) would address both.
